full_judgment:
8. Reilly, J, in Kallam Narayana vs Emperor. AIR 1933 Madras 233 could not fully endorse to the arguments of Spencer, J. and stated that there is one general rule which must never be forgotten, namely, that in making presumption of fact or in drawing inference of fact from evidence a Judge or a Jury must always have regard to all the known facts of the case. And that they must do because they are required to decide on all questions of fact as reason- able men. "When it is the duty of Judge or a jury to draw from evidence a reasonable inference, it is not their duty to find that there was no conceivable possibility other than the conclusion which they reach, It is not possible for reasonable men to conduct the affairs of life or make judicial decisions on questions of fact with mathematical certainty" Reilly, J. observed: 

 41. Mr MK Rahman, the learned Additional Attorney-General for the State respondents though has made submission to the effect that the very fact that these accused-appellants compelled the informant side under threat to make this আপোষ নামা”and not to give evidence against them before the tribunal-reasonably tells in favour of guilt of the accused-persons. That this fact of compelling the informant side under threat to execute this আপোষ নামা”creates a presumption also that if the prosecution witnesses had not been compelled not to give evidence against the accused persons before the tribunal they would have told the truth before the tribunal and would have proved the prosecution case. The learned Additional Attorney-General has submitted also that this আপোষ নামা” was taken into evidence in presence of the accused persons but none of the accused persons raised any objection against it and did not put a single question to the PW 11 who produced this আপোষ নামা”before the tribunal raising any question as to the genuineness of this আপোষ নামা”. The learned Additional Attorney-General has argued that in the circumstances this আপোষ নামা” can be legally relied on as genuine and therefore, the tribunal and the High Court Division did not commit any wrong in putting reliance on this আপোষ নামা” The learned Additional Attorney-General, however, could not refute the contention of the learned Counsel for the appellants that since this আপোষ নামা” was not brought to the notice of the accused-appellants while examining them under section 342 of the Criminal Procedure Code this cannot be relied on and for this defect the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence also cannot be sustained.
